title: Finite polynomial equations descend under directed tensor base change
statement: Let $I$ be a directed preorder, $(A_i)_{i\in I}$ a diagram of commutative rings with colimit $A$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], $i_0\in I$, and $B_0$ a commutative $A_{i_0}$-algebra. Let $n\in\mathbb N$ and let $U,V$ be finite sets. Put $P_0=B_0[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. For each $v\in V$ fix a polynomial $q_v\in P_0[z_u:u\in U]$. Write $P_i=(A_i\otimes_{A_{i_0}}B_0)[x]$ for $i\ge i_0$ and $P=(A\otimes_{A_{i_0}}B_0)[x]$, with coefficient maps $\kappa_i:P_0\to P_i$ and $\kappa:P_0\to P$ induced by $b\mapsto1\otimes b$. If a tuple $t\in P^U$ satisfies $q_v(\kappa,t)=0$ for every $v\in V$, then some $i\ge i_0$ admits a tuple $t_i\in P_i^U$ satisfying $q_v(\kappa_i,t_i)=0$ for every $v\in V$. No finite-presentation assumption on $B_0$ is required.

proof.text: Put S=A_{i₀}, restrict indices to the nonempty directed upper tail above i₀, and put P₀=B₀[x]. Mathlib MvPolynomial.rTensorAlgEquiv identifies A_i tensor_S P₀ with P_i, and A tensor_S P₀ with P. On 1 tensor p it equals the coefficientwise map κ_i (respectively κ); this is checked coefficientwise using coeff_rTensorAlgEquiv_tmul and coeff_map. Tensor transition ring maps are the linear rTensor maps on their underlying modules, by induction on pure tensors. Functoriality and cocone naturality give their composition and compatibility laws.

Move the colimit solution through the inverse polynomial tensor equivalence. Apply clause (1) of elementwise tensor-colimit descent to each of its finitely many entries. Choose a common upper bound of the representative stages (Finite.exists_le) within the upper tail. Tensor transition maps put all entries in one stage. Compatibility with coprojections shows their colimit images are exactly the original entries.

Evaluation commutes with any ring homomorphism: the two homomorphisms out of the polynomial ring agree on constants and variables (Mathlib MvPolynomial.map_eval₂Hom). The coefficient maps commute with transitions since the tensor maps send 1 tensor p to 1 tensor p. Therefore each evaluated equation at the chosen stage has zero colimit image.

Apply clause (2) of elementwise tensor-colimit descent to each of the finitely many evaluated equations. Choose a common upper bound of their vanishing stages and the tuple stage. The composition laws show that every equation value is zero after transition there. Evaluation compatibility makes the transitioned tuple a solution. Move its entries through the polynomial tensor equivalence to obtain the required tuple in P_i. For empty U or V, Finite.exists_le still applies because the upper tail is nonempty; no excluded edge cases arise.
